message:
docs: record the preview-skip work, including the two things it got wrong on the way

Docs only. No product, test, or build file is touched.

0.0.19 moves from open to "fixed, product picker unproven", and 0.0.20 is added for the updater
defect B1 closed -- it was latent before this task and would have become common because of it,
which is the reason it was not left in the ledger.

Two findings are written down as findings rather than folded into the summary, because both
change what a later reader should believe.

PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT is served by DWM on this OS: a window that never returns from WM_PRINT still
yields a thumbnail in ~24ms and its WM_PRINT counter stays at zero. That weakens the incident's
"LDPlayer did not answer" reading -- the window is never asked. It does NOT establish that a wait
inside DWM was the cause; both remain candidates, and the docs say so. The fix stands either way,
for the reason that is now the load-bearing one: a block there cannot be cancelled from user mode,
so only a process boundary can reclaim it.

And the control dispatcher is two, not one. TCP and UDP both serve on the same object when a
control port is configured, which made the first version of the budget a data race. The design
note claiming a concurrency cap of one is corrected to one per dispatcher, so two.

The measurements are recorded with what they do not cover: 1920x1080 costs 33ms median and 41.6ms
worst regardless of surface type, isolation adds about 39ms per preview, and UWP and real
application windows were never measured.

The regression is 83 of 87 exiting zero. The four are tools that need arguments or a live host,
and none of their sources were touched by this work -- stated that way rather than as "all pass",
because a count without that distinction is not a result.

Also recorded: the host process I leaked while trying the dispatcher experiment by hand, how it
was identified by path and ended by pid without touching the user's own, and the ordering the
test now uses so it cannot happen again.
